q: A library database stores members. Each member's complete record (one row) is best described as a…
why: A tuple is one complete row/record. The whole members table is the relation; each column is an attribute.

q: A film-rental database has a Movie table. Which field is the best primary key?
why: A primary key must be unique and non-null. MovieID is unique; titles and genres can repeat.

q: One author writes many books. Which key links the Book table back to the Author table?
why: The 'many' side (Book) holds a foreign key referencing the 'one' side (Author) primary key.

q: A table stores customer name, address and a repeating list of phone numbers in one cell. What's wrong?
options: It's not in 1NF — cells must be atomic
why: Repeating groups / multiple values in one cell violate 1NF. Split phone numbers into separate rows (or a Phone table).

q: In a composite-key table OrderDetail(OrderID, ProductID, ProductName), ProductName depends only on ProductID. Which normal form is violated?
why: ProductName depends on part of the composite key (ProductID) only — a partial dependency, so it must move to a Product table (2NF).

q: A Student table stores (StudentID, TutorID, TutorName). TutorName depends on TutorID, not StudentID. What should be done?
options: Move TutorName to a Tutor table (3NF)
why: TutorName is transitively dependent on StudentID via TutorID. Move it to a Tutor table to reach 3NF.

q: You try to add an Order with CustomerID 999, but no customer 999 exists. The DBMS should reject it because of…
why: Referential integrity requires a foreign key to match an existing primary key.

q: A small charity needs a single-user database on one office PC. Which is the most suitable choice?
why: Access is a desktop RDBMS ideal for small, single-user needs. Server databases suit many concurrent users.

q: You're designing a school database. In the conceptual ERD you would include…
why: Conceptual = high level (entities + relationships). Attributes, keys and types come in the logical model.

q: Which field would you make the primary key in an Employee table?
why: EmployeeID is unique and stable. Names, job titles and DOB can repeat or change.

q: On an order form, you want the user to pick a customer from a drop-down rather than type an ID. Use a…
why: A combo box lets users select from a list (often a lookup table), preventing invalid IDs.

q: You need a query that asks 'Enter minimum price:' and then lists products above it. This is a…
why: A parameter query prompts for a value at run time, making it reusable.

q: Testing an Age field with -5, 999 and 'abc' checks…
why: These invalid/edge values confirm validation rules reject bad input and boundary cases.

q: You ask three classmates to enter a new customer and give feedback. This is…
why: Usability testing gathers real-user feedback on how easy the forms/menus are to use.

q: Before submitting, you check the database still meets every point in the client's brief. This is…
why: Fitness for purpose verifies the solution against the original requirements — a C3 criterion.

q: Returning only the rows two tables have in common is the ______ operation.
why: Intersect returns common rows; union combines all rows; join merges on a shared attribute.

q: You set a rule that a Product's Price must be > 0. This is a…
why: A validation rule enforces a condition (Price > 0) before data is accepted.

q: Write the SQL to fetch every column from a table called Movie.
why: SELECT * FROM Movie retrieves all columns and rows. (Note: selecting only needed columns is better for optimisation.)

q: A query is slow. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Select only needed columns and index the join key
Store results in the same table
why: Selecting specific columns and indexing join keys reduce work — core query optimisation.

q: You can't add a new course until at least one student enrols on it. This design flaw is…
why: Insertion anomaly — unrelated data (a student) is required before you can insert the course.
